heroHeadline: Trump Cancels Planned May 19 Iran Strike at Gulf Allies' Request — War Day 80; Kentucky Primary: Gallrein vs. Massie MAGA Test; Cuba Sanctions on 11 Officials
heroSubtitle: President Trump announced on May 19, 2026 (War Day 80) that he called off a scheduled military strike on Iran planned for Tuesday after Saudi Arabia, the UAE, and Qatar personally requested he hold off because 'serious negotiations are now taking place' — one day after Trump had warned Iran to 'get moving, FAST.' US officials characterized Iran's revised 14-point counter-proposal (submitted to Pakistani mediators) as 'not a meaningful improvement,' and Trump directed his military to remain 'prepared for a full, large-scale assault on a moment's notice.' The central negotiating gap remains: the US demands a 10–12 year enrichment moratorium plus surrender of Iran's ~440 kg of highly-enriched uranium, while Iran has offered only a 5-year suspension. The Strait of Hormuz naval blockade continues with ~41 tankers blocked and Brent crude at ~$107/bbl. On the political front, polls closed May 19 in the Kentucky 4th District Republican primary — the most expensive House primary in US history at $32M+ in ad spending — where Trump-backed challenger Ed Gallrein (former Navy SEAL) faced seven-term incumbent Rep. Thomas Massie; final polls showed Gallrein ahead 48.3% to 43.1% in a test of Trump's ~82% primary endorsement win rate against a defiant incumbent. On Cuba, the Trump administration imposed new sanctions on 11 Cuban government officials and 3 security agencies, with Secretary Rubio warning more designations are coming. On immigration, a Brookings Institution report estimated 100,000+ US-born children have been separated from detained parents — with no ICE protocol to protect them — as the administration simultaneously proposed raising the Afrikaner refugee cap from 7,500 to 17,500.
